ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left figure shows a square sheet of paper, with a diagonal drawn from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner; the curved arrows indicate that the two adjacent sides, the bottom side and the right side, are folded onto this diagonal. In the right figure, the red border is the protruding quadrilateral obtained after folding. Reasoning: Let the lower-right corner of the square be O. Each fold folds a side passing through O onto the same diagonal, so the corresponding crease is the angle bisector of the angle between that side and the diagonal. The angles between the square's diagonal and the bottom side and the right side are both 45°, so the angle between each crease and the corresponding side is 22.5°. For the small right triangle at the lower-left corner formed by folding the bottom side, the base length is 1, the height is tan(22.5°)=√2−1, so the area is (1/2)(√2−1). The small triangle cut off at the upper-right corner is congruent to it, with the same area. Therefore the required area of the red quadrilateral is equal to the area of the unit square minus the areas of these two triangles: 1−2·(1/2)(√2−1)=1−(√2−1)=2−√2.

method.method_draft: Use the diagram to identify the folded sides as the bottom and right sides of a unit square, both folded onto the same diagonal from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner. Name the bottom-right corner O. Each fold crease starts at O and is the angle bisector between the side being folded and the diagonal. Since the diagonal makes a 45° angle with each side, each crease cuts off a small right triangle whose acute angle at O is 22.5°. For the lower-left cutoff triangle, its base is 1 and its height along the left side is tan(22.5°)=sqrt(2)-1. The upper-right cutoff triangle is congruent. The highlighted quadrilateral is the unit square minus these two congruent triangles, so its area is 1 - 2*(1/2)*(sqrt(2)-1) = 2 - sqrt(2).

method.method_draft: Model one fold by reflection rather than angles. Label the square with bottom-left D, bottom-right C, top-left A, top-right B, and diagonal AC. The bottom side DC folds onto diagonal AC, so D is reflected to a point P on AC with CP=CD=1. Since AC has length sqrt(2), P is one unit from C along the diagonal. Let E be where the crease meets the left side AD. Because E lies on the fold crease, it is equidistant from D and its reflected image P, so ED=EP. Put coordinates D=(0,0), C=(1,0), A=(0,1). Then P=(1-1/sqrt(2), 1/sqrt(2)) and E=(0,h). Solve h=EP, giving h=sqrt(2)-1. Thus the lower-left triangle cut off has area h/2. By symmetry, the upper-right fold cuts off another equal triangle. Therefore the highlighted quadrilateral has area 1 - h = 1 - (sqrt(2)-1) = 2 - sqrt(2).
